intelligence.enrichment: Transparent materials allow things to be seen clearly through them. Translucent materials allow objects to be seen but not clearly. Opaque materials do not allow objects to be seen through them at all. clarity of seeing through a material -> transparent, translucent, or opaque classification The learner correctly applies this rule: Transparent materials allow things to be seen clearly through them. Translucent materials allow objects to be seen but not clearly. Opaque materials do not allow objects to be seen through them at all. Anything made of glass is transparent, so frosted glass must be transparent.

spec.instruction: Write one new grades 6 Science question. Chapter: Materials around us. The student must decide: When looking through a material, decide whether it is transparent, translucent, or opaque from how clearly objects can be seen. Use an Indian school or home setting and Indian names. Keep the source language register. Retarget the source onto this Science decision. Keep the source item type. Recalculate the key.
